parts.label: (a)
parts.stem:
An aldehyde, an alkane and a carboxylic acid, all of similar volatility, are mixed together. The mixture is then analysed in a gas chromatograph.

The gas chromatogram produced is shown.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

The separation of the compounds depends on their relative solubilities in the stationary phase. The stationary phase is a liquid alcohol.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text:
Complete the table to suggest which compound in the mixture is responsible for each peak $\mathbf{X}$, $\mathbf{Y}$ and $\mathbf{Z}$. Explain your answer by reference to the intermolecular forces of the compounds.

| peak | organic compound | explanation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $\mathbf{X}$ |  |  |
| $\mathbf{Y}$ |  |  |
| $\mathbf{Z}$ |  |  |

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
A student calculates the areas underneath the three peaks in the chromatogram.

| peak | $\mathbf{X}$ | $\mathbf{Y}$ | $\mathbf{Z}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| area/$\text{mm}^2$ | 19 | 32 | 47 |

The area underneath each peak is proportional to the mass of the respective compound.

Calculate the percentage **by mass** in the original mixture of the compound responsible for peak $\mathbf{Z}$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
The mass spectrum of a halogenoalkane containing one chlorine atom **or** bromine atom will show an additional peak at M+2.

State the isotopes of chlorine and bromine responsible for M+2 peaks.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
The mass spectrum of bromochloromethane, $\text{CH}_2\text{BrCl}$, has a molecular ion peak, M, at an $m/e$ value of 128. It also has M+2 and M+4 peaks.

Suggest the identity of the molecular ions that give rise to these peaks.

parts.label: (c)
(c)(i)
parts.text: Draw the mechanism of this reaction. Include all relevant curly arrows, dipoles and charges.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
1-bromo-2-methylpropane is also formed in this reaction.

Explain why 2-bromo-2-methylpropane will be the **major** product in this reaction.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by the term *partition coefficient*, $K_{\text{partition}}$.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
The partition coefficient of organic compound $\mathbf{H}$ between dichloromethane and water is 4.75.

- $2.50\text{ g}$ of compound $\mathbf{H}$ was dissolved in water and made up to $100\text{ cm}^3$ in a volumetric flask.
- $50\text{ cm}^3$ of this aqueous solution were shaken with $10\text{ cm}^3$ of dichloromethane.

Calculate the mass of compound $\mathbf{H}$ that was extracted into the dichloromethane.
